messages:
jordan: Heads-up — deploy-bot shows an unpin for runtime v2.14 -> v2.15 scheduled for canary at 09:15 UTC. Notified teams.
deploy-bot: Scheduled action: UNPIN runtime v2.14 -> v2.15 (canary). Trigger: nightly-release-window. ETA: 09:15 UTC.
maya: Hold on, we have a failing integration in nightly that looks like a bind/regression with the new runtime+SDK binding.
maya: Test: Integration::kvcache_bind failing consistently on longseq runs.
qa-liz: Yep I saw that. Repro steps in staging: `./scripts/run_integration.sh --profile longseq --model llama3q --runtime v2.15`
maya: Failing snippet:
```
E 0x7f9c2c: bind_kernel(): mismatch: expected kernel "kv_cache_bind_v3" but runtime provided "kv_cache_bind_v2"
AssertionError: kernel-version-mismatch
```
maya: This suggests the runtime selected a different kernel path for quantized models. Could be a kernel selection table change in 2.15.
tim: @maya can you dump the runtime kernel table from the failing container? `cat /proc/runtime/kernels.json` should show what it picked.
maya: Pasted output to gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/abcd1234 (short list, kernel entries show v2 not v3 for llama3q)
jordan: If this is real, unpin will break canary traffic for a subset of models. We should pause the unpin until we confirm.
sre-oncall: Agreed. Impact looks limited to quantized llama3q longseq path, but that’s used by 2 internal customers. Recommend hold and escalate to runtime team.
product-kate: Customer-facing risk: two active customers in EU onboarding using longseq. We should notify account owners if we hold beyond 30m.
deploy-bot: Actionable: PAUSE unpin action for thread 2388881234. Reason: pending kernel-binding regression investigation. (requested by jordan)
jordan: Proposed immediate plan:
- Hold unpin for canary now.
- Runtime team triage: confirm kernel-selection delta and whether it's a config vs code change.
- If patch available within 2h, re-run canary with targeted subset of models.
- If not, roll back the runtime release PR and keep previous pinned version.
maya: Triage notes: diff between v2.14 and v2.15 shows change to kernel lookup fallback order in compile.cc (line ~412). Quick revert locally fixes the test.
maya: Patch: revert fallback order or add explicit kernel alias mapping. I can open a hotfix PR, but it needs runtime approval and a canary build.
tim: @maya please open PR and add `runtime-team` and `eng-releases` labels. Also add a small smoketest step in CI for longseq+llama3q.
maya: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/1834 — title: "fix: kernel alias fallback for kv_cache_bind (llama3q longseq)"
qa-liz: I'll queue a canary deployment once CI has the PR build. ETA for CI: ~35m.
product-kate: I'll draft a short status note for the two customers in case we extend hold beyond 30m.
jordan: Decision: HOLD unpin for canary. If hotfix lands and CI green within 90m, attempt scoped canary to 5% model cohort. If not, rollback release PR and unblock later.
sre-oncall: I'll update the incident channel and watch telemetry. Also set alert to notify if error rate for longseq > 1% after any future canary.
maya: I'll post updates here when CI finishes.
deploy-bot: Confirmed: UNPIN action paused. Waiting on manual resume by eng-releases.
maya: CI green ✅ (2388882500). Built canary image with PR#1834.
qa-liz: Scoped canary deploy started at 09:45 UTC to 5% of canary fleet, models: llama3q-quant-*, longseq profile only.
jordan: Monitoring: no bind errors in first 10m, token latency stable.
product-kate: I'll hold customer notifications for now, will notify only if we extend hold.
tim: If canary stays clean for 30m, we can resume full unpin. Otherwise we'll roll back the release PR.
qa-liz: Canary passed 30m window. No regressions seen.
jordan: Resume unpin at 10:35 UTC. @deploy-bot please proceed with the remaining canary wave and then full roll.
deploy-bot: Resuming UNPIN: proceeding with staged canary -> remaining canary -> regional rollouts per schedule.
product-kate: Notifying customers: "we resumed the canary after a quick fix; no impact observed".
jordan: Closing thread. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
